Archive:376YE Winter Solstice Imperial t.d: Each Imperial territory's senator and each army's general were listed. League bishops took four cardinalships (Ambition, Loyalty, Prosperity and The Way), and Gralka of the Imperial Orcs became Conscience of the Senate. Six archmagi were declared, and the order grandmasters were to serve with fixed voting strengths until the Spring Equinox 377YE. Because of concerns about economic stability in a time of Imperial crisis, Bourse seats won at this summit were to run until Winter 377YE. The Brilliant Shore, the Great Forest at Reikos and the Great Pits of Ennerlund were held by Thule and the Druj and would not be auctioned until their territories were Imperial again.

n.Dawn: Dawn's three senators were listed, along with Generals Floree de Rondell, Eryk Rykker and Frederick Novarion of the Hounds of Glory, Golden Sun and Eastern Sky.
n.Druj: The Druj held the Great Forest at Reikos and the Great Pits of Ennerlund, and neither would be auctioned until Reikos and Holberg were Imperial again.
n.Highguard: Highguard's senators and Generals Matthias and Ruth were listed, alongside gatekeepers Asher (Courage) and Abraham (Vigilance), Grandmaster Jessica of the Sevenfold Path and Obediah holding the Vigilant Swan.
n.Imperial Orcs: Generals Klor of the Winter Sun and Braka of the Summer Storm sat on the Military Council, and Gralka was appointed Conscience of the Senate.
n.Navarr: Alongside its senators and two generals, Navarr provided the Cardinals of Courage and Wisdom, the Pride gatekeeper, Grandmaster Meir Pathfinder of the Rod and Shield and the holder of the Thimble.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn senators were listed, with Madruga's seat later proxied by Yalda i Ezmara i Erigo. Generals Yasmina and Deigo were also listed, and Darius i Esmara i Erigo became gatekeeper of the Prosperity Assembly.
n.The League: The League dominated the Synod with four cardinalships and held many Imperial Bourse seats, the Regario Dossier and the Mastery of the Imperial Mint. Its senators and General Stanislav Krieger of the Wolves of War were also listed.
n.The Marches: Marcher Langdon Tor became Cardinal of Pride, and Silent John and Alan Young were made gatekeepers. William Bolholt led the Golden Pyramid with a voting strength of 76, and the Marches' senators and three generals were listed.
n.Thule: Thule held the Brilliant Shore, which would not be auctioned until Skarsind was once again an Imperial territory.
n.Urizen: Urizen's three senators were listed, along with General Decius Cascade of the Citadel Guard and Valerion of Phoenix Reach, who held the Legacy.
n.Varushka: Varushka gained the Cardinal of Vigilance and the Wisdom gatekeeper, and Alexei became Grandmaster of the Unfettered Mind. It also held two national Bourse seats, and its senators and two generals were listed.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's senators were listed, along with Generals Merrick and Erkenbrand of the Green Shield and Fist of the Mountain, and Wyrda Bjornadottir, Grandmaster of the Shuttered Lantern with a voting strength of 63.

Construct Madruga shipyard.d: The motion was proposed by the senator for Sarvos and seconded by the senator for Madruga. Construction required 35 wains of white granite and 5 wains of weirwood, with an upkeep of 5 thrones. Mirislav, Senator for Sarvos, paid the costs during the Spring Equinox 377YE downtime. Once built, the shipyard means that every Freeborn fleet operating out of Madruga produces more wealth for its owner. The total benefit is 720 rings per season, divided among all the fleets active in Madruga that season.

n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn fleet owners sailing from Madruga share an extra 720 rings each season from the new shipyard, strengthening the nation's maritime wealth.
n.The League: The League's senator for Sarvos proposed the shipyard and then paid its construction costs, effectively funding a Freeborn project.

t.Madruga: Madruga gains a new Imperial shipyard, and the fleets operating from it share 720 additional rings of wealth each season.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos's senator, Mirislav, proposed the motion and personally paid the materials for a shipyard built in another territory.

Construct shrine for Britta's body.d: Proposed by the senator for Necropolis and seconded by Sermersuaq, the motion passed with 7 thrones and 12 votes against, the money going to Necropolis. Construction cost 10 white granite, paid by Adamah, Senator for Necropolis, in the Spring Equinox downtime. The resulting sinecure, Guardian of Britta's Shrine, yields 10 Synod votes and 5 liao. Ruth of the Cenotaph was appointed by the Highborn, and future holders are chosen by unanimous decision of the Highguard senators. Because a Senate-appointed title grants Synod votes, giving the Senate undue influence over the Synod, it is regarded as unconstitutional. The magistrates did not strike it down at the time, and the construction has been completed.

n.Highguard: The Highguard senators control the new Guardian of Britta's Shrine title and must agree unanimously on future holders. Its first holder, Ruth of the Cenotaph, was appointed by the Highborn and gains 10 Synod votes and 5 liao from the sinecure.

t.Necropolis: Necropolis became the resting place of Empress Britta's effects and the site of a monument. Its senator proposed the motion and paid the 10 white granite for its construction.

Fortify Town defences.d: Proposed by the Senator for Mitwold and seconded by the Senator for Temeschwar, the motion passed at 60 Thrones with 13 votes against, and the money went to Senator Mitwold. Full fortification needed 300 wains of White Granite, but 40 wains were enough to suppress banditry. Bridget Eastville née Talbot, Senator for Mitwold, presented 40 wains in the Winter Solstice 2013 downtime. Meade, Sybela and Mellfort were partially fortified, which ended the banditry problems but gave no military advantage. Completing all three would take another 260 wains. The motion broke constitutional protocol by covering more than one item, but magistrates did not strike it down and construction went ahead.

n.Highguard: Highguard was one of the three nations whose towns the motion sought to fortify, and banditry there was suppressed once the partial fortifications were built.
n.The League: League towns benefited from the partial fortifications, which suppressed banditry in the League, and the motion was seconded by the Senator for Temeschwar.
n.The Marches: The Marches led the motion through Mitwold's senator, Bridget Eastville née Talbot, who received the funds and presented the 40 wains of White Granite that suppressed banditry in the nation.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: Bastion is not named; the page refers only generally to towns in Highguard being fortified against banditry.
t.Mitwold: Mitwold's senator proposed the motion, received the Thrones and delivered the 40 wains of White Granite that paid for the work.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar's senator seconded the motion to fortify League, Marcher and Highborn towns.

Raise Highguard army.d: Raised by the senator for Hercynia and seconded by Necropolis, the motion passed at 120 thrones with 9 votes against. The army required 150 wains of mithril and a year to construct, though the page notes it should have cost 250 wains. Adamah, Senator for Necropolis, supplied the full 150 wains of mithril over the course of 376YE. The result was to be a new Highborn army, whose general would be appointed by the Highborn senators through the standard procedure once it was complete.

n.Highguard: Highguard gained a new army of its own, with its general to be chosen by the Highborn senators once construction was complete.

t.Necropolis: Necropolis seconded the motion and received the money for the work, and its senator Adamah supplied all 150 wains of mithril needed to build the army.
